 "clustering_entrances": [
  {
   "entrance": "Gestalt proximity: things set close belong together",
   "spw_constructs": "Tight vs open act-bound spacing (flow-protocol-sigils.spw:44-49: tight = high commitment, spaced = softer aperture; adjacency resonates). The gap classes in spw inspect spacing are tight, open, cadence (line break) and episode (blank line).",
   "why_it_fits": "Designers already read gaps. In Spw the gap is sometimes grammar (verified: a bias edge exists only in the tight form), which turns an optical instinct into a structural probe."
  },
  {
   "entrance": "Common region / closure: a box groups what it encloses",
   "spw_constructs": "{} bodies, ^[\"frame\"]{} named frames, and the four containers that answer structuring questions (operator-atlas.spw:25-31: [] parts, {} properties, () who is looking, <> what it might become)",
   "why_it_fits": "Braces are drawn regions. The container a designer picks says which question the group answers."
  },
  {
   "entrance": "Layers panel and frame nesting",
   "spw_constructs": "Nested ^[] frames (depth 3 verified in every sketch). The LSP breadcrumb framePath follows ^ frames only, not .{} (tags.md F7).",
   "why_it_fits": "This maps directly onto the layers-panel habit, as long as .{} is kept for leaf property panels that do not appear in the breadcrumb."
  },
  {
   "entrance": "Properties panel, component variants, and design styles",
   "spw_constructs": "Leaf properties go in .{ size: large, state: hover } facets (Bindings, verified). Classification goes in #:axis #!value particle stacks (header axes from vocabulary.spw:29-38).",
   "why_it_fits": "A variant is a property = value pair. The facet holds the values and the particle pair classifies the thing, the way Figma separates variant properties from style tags."
  },
  {
   "entrance": "Gestalt similarity: same color or shape means same kind",
   "spw_constructs": "Shared concept tags ^[\"concepts\"]{ primary: [#tag] } that recur across files. The LSP Concepts tree shows co-occurrence (tags.md rec 4). Recurring ~#name(…) apposition keys are counted by spw lattice.",
   "why_it_fits": "Similarity becomes a shared mark. vocabulary.spw:3 says a value 'earns its place by recurring', which matches how a style earns a swatch."
  },
  {
   "entrance": "Component sets, swatch groups, grid columns",
   "spw_constructs": "#[ a ; b ; c ] sets (operators.spw:97, :119), verified with identifiers and numbers",
   "why_it_fits": "A set is a category, the grouping a designer makes when naming a family."
  },
  {
   "entrance": "Auto-layout stacks, timelines, x-sheets, keyframe tracks",
   "spw_constructs": "<< a ; b >> sequential and << a || b >> parallel Stream schedules (flow-protocol-sigils.spw:33, :48)",
   "why_it_fits": "Order and parallel tracks map one to one. Timing is written as explicit values beside them."
  },
  {
   "entrance": "Moodboards and Warburg-style picture panels",
   "spw_constructs": "Plates: pins as ~\"file.spw#anchor\" lists, prefix coupling <>[a, b], a ~#reading(…) apposition, and a required breaks: binding (designers/affinity-panel.spw)",
   "why_it_fits": "A moodboard is a set of pinned references grouped by affinity. Plates keep the pins addressable, so spw resolve checks them, and every pairing carries the limit that cli.spw:49 demands."
  },
  {
   "entrance": "Visual hierarchy: rank of emphasis",
   "spw_constructs": "Tight bias edges =~\"a.spw#x\"[axis]{ ~\"b.spw#y\" ; ~\"c.spw#z\" }, which readBias ranks in order and which =bane inverts (syntax_breadth F7; linking.md F11)",
   "why_it_fits": "A ranked target list reads as a hierarchy of references. It is the only typed, ranked relation the tools honor today."
  },
  {
   "entrance": "Design tokens and style libraries",
   "spw_constructs": "Registry cells %ns.key{ value, unit, at, rel|abs, src, status } under a ^[\"family\"] declaration (registries/quantities/matter.spw:20-41; contract.spw:84-90). Canon's --quality-* CSS variables (valence-architecture.spw:45-81).",
   "why_it_fits": "A named value with a unit, a source and a status is a token with provenance. Files read handles instead of restating numbers."
  },
  {
   "entrance": "Prototype flows and linking to a node",
   "spw_constructs": "#> anchors plus ~\"file#anchor\" trails, and reading-order schedules in a door index (designers/index.spw ^[\"by_hand\"])",
   "why_it_fits": "A prototype flow is a path through anchored frames. A door lays one path per sub-role."
  },
  {
   "entrance": "Material boards (industrial design)",
   "spw_constructs": "#:valence #!x particles, one per face reading, bound to the next binding (verified), with a %spectrum{…_share} facet",

   "spw_constructs": "The / projection chain (operators.spw:116, :167), verified as Expression(/ /)",
   "why_it_fits": "Slash-path variant naming is already a projection from general to specific."
  },
  {
   "entrance": "Breakpoints and viewport contexts",
   "spw_constructs": "@name(word){…} perspective scope (operators.spw:36, :99)",
   "why_it_fits": "A breakpoint is a viewpoint. Write it as a named perspective with a word, never as key: value inside the parens, where the key is dropped."
  }
 ],
 "contraptions": [
  {
   "name": "Kerning Specimen",
   "what_it_explores": "Where a gap between marks changes the parse tree. It sets pairs once tight and once open, with a control pair where the gap does not matter and a line-break pair where a unit capsule reaches across lines. Gestalt proximity becomes grammar you can measure.",
   "spw_sketch": "#>kern_bias_tight\n^[\"bias_tight\"]{\n =~\"./kerning.spw#kern_target\"[near]{ ~\"./kerning.spw#kern_target\" }\n}\n#>kern_bias_open\n^[\"bias_open\"]{\n =[near] ~\"./kerning.spw\" { ~\"./kerning.spw#kern_target\" }\n}\n^[\"couple\"]{\n tight: <>[figure, ground]\n open: figure <> ground\n}\n^[\"rule_control\"]{\n tight: .card{ radius: 8 }\n open: .card { radius: 8 }\n}\n#>kern_target\n^[\"target\"]{ note: \"the landing anchor for the bias rows\" }",
   "parses": true,
   "exists_today": "Verified with existing commands on scratchpad/persona/designers/excerpts/kerning.spw and designers/kerning-specimen.spw. The validator passes. readBias via archcheck finds 1 edge (tight row only). spw fingerprint --expr gives different signatures for the tight and open coupling (Frame=1 Parameter=2 vs ModifierChain=1) and the same signature for both .card rows. spw inspect spacing classifies every gap as tight, open, cadence or episode.",
   "tooling_needed": "The readings work with existing CLI (spw fingerprint, spw inspect spacing, spw select). New: a pairs mode, for example spw inspect spacing --pairs or a spw specimen verb, that takes anchored tight/open rows and prints the fingerprint diff and bias-edge diff side by side. Also a gate check that flags cross-line capsules and open bias forms.",
   "wonder": "Whitespace turns out to be a typographic variable with semantic weight. Designers can find where the language is 'kerned', where a space splits one act into two, and where it is only optical."
  },
  {
   "name": "Golden Grid",
   "what_it_explores": "Snapping marks at a pitch onto a whole-unit grid leaves a word of long and short gaps. Rational pitches repeat: 3/2 every 2 marks, 8/5 every 5, 13/8 every 8. The golden pitch never repeats and spells the Fibonacci word, the one-dimensional model used for quasicrystals. The continued-fraction ladder of pitches walks visibly toward aperiodic order.",
   "spw_sketch": "^[\"pitches\"]{\n #>grid_pitch_eight_fifths\n ^[\"eight_fifths\"]{ pitch: 1.6, marks: 34 }\n #>grid_pitch_golden\n ^[\"golden\"]{ pitch: 1.6180339887, marks: 34 }\n}\n#>grid_golden_fibonacci\n^[\"golden_word\"]{\n #:claim #!settled\n statement: \"At the golden pitch the gap word has no period and spells the Fibonacci word, where each L becomes LS and each S becomes L.\"\n ^[\"limits\"]{ fails: \"a stored pitch is a decimal and so rational; 1.6180339887 repeats only after ten billion marks\" }\n}\n#>grid_quasicrystal_q\n?[\"Is a golden grid a one-dimensional quasicrystal a designer can draw?\"]{\n #:depth #!mathematical ~#lens(formal structure)\n !probe{ \"test every period from 1 to 16 across the whole word\" =id[p_design_grid_period] =kind[calc] }\n breaks: \"a quasicrystal is three-dimensional atomic order seen through diffraction; the grid word shares only the sequence\"\n}",
   "parses": true,
   "exists_today": "The full surface designers/golden-grid.spw and the excerpt both pass. Scratch prototype designers-tools/contraptions.mts reads the pitches from the AST. It computes words with true periods 2, 5, 8 and none within 16, and the golden word matches the Fibonacci substitution prefix. Finding: the seed's detectPeriod (math/loop.ts:107) only compares the last two windows. It gives false positives on these words: periods 3 and 8 for the golden word, period 1 for 8/5.",
   "tooling_needed": "New: a word family in seed math. It needs a full-window period test (complementing detectPeriod), a Beatty/Sturmian generator and a substitution comparison. Register it as a spw formula catalog entry (for example grid.snap), declare a design quantity family for pitches, and add a bar-strip view of the L/S word as an atlas or emit projection. orbit (math/loop.ts:94) already covers modular type-scale ladders.",
   "wonder": "The eye cannot tell 1.6 from 1.618 in a layout, yet one repeats every 5 marks and the other never repeats. A designer can draw aperiodic order by hand, and a plate can pin it beside a matter surface on quasicrystals (Shechtman et al. 1984, in sources.spw)."
  },
  {
   "name": "Valence Spectrum",
   "what_it_explores": "Materials read by five charge-neutral faces: rest (bone), limit (bane), irreversible shift (bonk), opening (boon), signal (honk). Canon's own rule is that no two components should share a fingerprint (valence-architecture.spw:95). The spectrum asks whether two materials with equal shares still ask for different hands.",
   "spw_sketch": "#>spectrum_clay\n^[\"clay\"]{\n #:valence #!bone\n rest: \"a plastic body that holds a thrown form\"\n #:valence #!bane\n limit: \"shrinks as it dries and fires, so uneven walls crack\"\n #:valence #!bonk\n shift: \"vitrifies in the kiln, and the change does not reverse\"\n #:valence #!boon\n opening: \"takes glaze, texture, and fingerprints\"\n %spectrum{ boon_share: 0.25, bane_share: 0.25, bone_share: 0.25, bonk_share: 0.25, honk_share: 0 }\n}",
   "parses": true,
   "exists_today": "designers/valence-spectrum.spw (clay, molded plywood, neon) and the excerpt pass. archcheck confirms each #:valence #!x pair binds to the reading below it. The scratch recount in contraptions.mts reads faces from the particles: declared shares match the recount with 0.000 drift and there are no twins (the closest pair, clay and plywood, differ by 0.25). The valence keys use *_share because a bare boon: key degrades the file (verified).",
   "tooling_needed": "New: a lint or measure rule that recounts #:valence faces per anchored frame against the declared %spectrum shares, and a twin finder. Register a spectrum family in registries/quantities/design.spw using the ^[\"family\"] form from quantities/matter.spw:20-30. Add a panel view that lays out five unordered swatches using canon's --quality-* variables and never interpolates between them.",
   "wonder": "Industrial designers get one panel where clay, molded plywood, neon, and water's own structure and phase change sit side by side. The canon rule 'no two identical fingerprints' becomes a checkable claim. It also raises a question: do Spw's own operators have spectra too?"
  },
  {
   "name": "X-Sheet Commutator",
   "what_it_explores": "Row order on an exposure sheet is composition order. Turn-then-move differs from move-then-turn, while turn and uniform grow about one pivot commute. This is group theory felt in a timeline, and it mirrors canon's open question about which operator pairs do not commute (register-geometry.spw:120-132: !(~x) may differ from ~(!x)).",
   "spw_sketch": "#>xsheet_rows\n^[\"row_pairs\"]{\n turn_then_move: << rotate ; translate >>\n move_then_turn: << translate ; rotate >>\n turn_then_grow: << rotate ; scale >>\n grow_then_turn: << scale ; rotate >>\n #>xsheet_commute\n ^[\"commutation\"]{\n  #:claim #!settled\n  statement: \"Rows on one layer commute only when their transforms do: rotation and uniform scale about one pivot do, rotation and translation do not.\"\n }\n}",
   "parses": true,
   "exists_today": "Schedules parse as ordered Stream sequences (verified). The scratch evaluator in contraptions.mts reads the rows from the AST and applies them to a unit square. Turn/move gives corners [[1,0],[1,1],[0,1],[0,0]] vs [[0,1],[0,2],[-1,2],[-1,1]], so they differ. Turn/grow gives identical corners, so they commute. This corrected the prior draft's hypothesis, and the correction is recorded in the xsheet provenance. The ball-bounce frame's spacing [0, 0.04, 0.16, 0.36, 0.64, 1] is the square of evenly spaced times.",
   "tooling_needed": "New: a small 2D affine evaluator over schedule rows (rotate, translate, scale, with the pivot declared), plus onion-skin output. For operator pairs, canon's own test (register-geometry.spw:123: compare parse, ONF, runtime value, register writes, trace order) needs a runtime-trace diff command. spw beat exists for cadence ticks but computes no geometry.",
   "wonder": "Animators discover they have been doing non-abelian algebra all along. The same 'does order matter?' question becomes a probe of Spw's own operator algebra, with the timeline as the instrument."
  }
 ],
 "doors": [

   "why": "This starts from recognition instead of jargon. Every analogy sits beside an observable and a stated limit, as cli.spw:45-51 and operator-atlas.spw:17 require.",

 "architecture_recs": [
  "Add doors/ at the cut root (doors/design.spw, doors/physics.spw, …). Each door is an index that only routes: a ^[\"tree\"] of links plus a ^[\"by_hand\"] reading-order schedule per sub-role. The shape is verified in designers/index.spw. Doors never restate content.",
  "Add one glossary lattice beside vocabulary.spw (glossary.spw, or glossary/<persona>.spw) with rows of sigil, canon, <persona>_analog, observable, breaks, anchored #>gloss_<persona>_<mark>. The gate should reject any *_analog without an observable and a breaks sibling. That makes the cli.spw:49 metaphor boundary and the register-geometry.spw:26 falsifier checkable.",
  "Add specimens/: sheets of tight/open pairs and hazard pairs (hex, >, negative numbers, :hover, @x(k: v), valence keys, unit capsules, curly quotes). Label each with its expected parser verdict so they double as gate fixtures. The gate must read parse().errors, because spw-syntax-validate prints ✓ on files with dropped signs and characters (verified in p4 and bez.spw).",
  "Add plates/: Warburg-style link-only surfaces that pin anchors from at least two branches with <>[a, b], a ~#reading(…) apposition, and a required breaks: binding (designers/affinity-panel.spw ^[\"plate_rule\"]). Plates are where design meets matter, physics and animation, and spw resolve --warn checks every pin.",
  "Add contraptions/: one surface per contraption holding its parameters (pitches, row pairs, material faces), its claims with limits, one wonder, and a tool: binding naming the existing command or proposed analyzer, with status #proposed until the tool exists. Put the prototype receipts beside it (for example, the output of designers-tools/contraptions.mts).",
  "Add registries/quantities/design.spw so design numbers such as fps, hold frames, grid pitches and the spectrum family live in the same ^[\"family\"] plus %ns.key{ value, unit, at, src, status } cells as matter (quantities/matter.spw:20-41), with sources in registries/sources/design.spw. Contraptions then read handles instead of restating numbers (contract.spw:84-88).",
  "Add design (and each live branch) to the domain axis in vocabulary.spw:31, which currently lists only meta and matter. Add forms such as specimen and plate only once they recur (vocabulary.spw:3).",
  "Resolve the anchor-namespace tension. contract.spw:59 wants the domain slug first, but spw atlas groups anchors by the first [a-z]+ segment. The designer sketches showed families gloss, kern, design and grid. Either teach atlas a two-segment namespace (design_grid_*) or allow contraption-first anchors inside a domain folder, so the visual atlas shows contraptions as families.",
  "Use ^[] frames for anything that should appear in the editor breadcrumb or layers view, and keep .{} for leaf property panels. That is the split the LSP honors today (tags.md F7), so the designer's layers-panel model matches the tool.",
  "Write every number that is not a plain integer or decimal in a single form: .{ n: 24, unit: \"px\" } for quantities, strings for negatives, colors and ratios (contract.spw:89; water.spw:133). The same form then serves physics units and design units, and it avoids every verified split and swallow.",
  "Cross design contraptions into materials on purpose. Give golden-grid an analog edge to a matter/quasicrystals surface, run the valence spectrum over matter surfaces (water's hydrogen-bond network as bone, its phase change as bonk), and point x-sheet at register-geometry's non-commutative pairs. Then exploring language design and exploring materials share one set of instruments.",
  "Add a language/ branch in the cut where Spw's own marks are the material: specimen sheets, the glossary lattice, and operator spectra (each operator's boon/bane/bone/bonk/honk faces, following valence-architecture.spw:47-83's per-component reading). The contraptions that explore clay and quasicrystals then also explore the language.",
  "Add visual projections of the tree as views, not new sources. spw atlas --html already exists. Propose a plate view (a grid of pinned anchors with breaks), a spectrum view (five unordered swatches using --quality-* variables), a specimen view (tight/open fingerprints side by side), and an L/S bar strip for the golden grid, as atlas modes or emit hosts."
 ],
 "theory_questions": [
  "Should hex colors have a literal form, or should a hex-shaped # operation be a lint error? Today a letter-led hex is a topic tag and a digit-led hex is a prose payload (verified).",
  "Should a stray > outside a capsule fail locally instead of degrading the whole surface to prose? It is one CSS-habit keystroke (verified sib3.spw).",
  "Should signed numbers, unit suffixes (120ms, 50%, 45°) and ratios (16/9, 1:1.618) become literals? Designers and physics students both need them, and today they split or lose their sign silently.",
  "Is the valence pentad ordered or categorical? Canon calls the combination a 'spectral signature' (valence-architecture.spw:95, :100), and spectra are ordered by wavelength. If valences are unordered categories, should 'spectral' go, or should an order be declared?",
  "Is canon's CSS projection of valence (css_var --quality-* at valence-architecture.spw:45-81, and the shader reading at :120-131) normative, a design-token contract a consumer can rely on, or illustrative?",
  "Should 'no two components should have identical fingerprints' (valence-architecture.spw:95) become a checkable measure? If so, what counts as a face, and does the order in which a maker meets the faces belong in the measure?",
  "Which meaning keeps the word 'fingerprint': spw fingerprint's AST node-type signature, or canon's valence spread?",
  "Should the editor show spacing-sensitive meaning, for example a semantic token or inlay when an open gap splits an act from its bound? Designers read space as optical, not grammatical (flow-protocol-sigils.spw:44-47).",
  "Should () scopes keep bindings? @viewport(max_width: 600) silently drops the key while keeping 600.",
  "Should the particle run written first inside a body describe that container (container deixis), matching how designers label a group from its top edge? Today it binds to the next node.",
  "Is it intended that .{} facets stay out of the editor frame path while ^ frames appear, or should facets be visible layers too?",
  "Could render-only orientation (operators.spw:85-90: left, right, inward, outward, accumulate, release, with the invariant that tokens, AST, ONF and effects are preserved) become a sanctioned visual layer where designers restyle braces and glyph direction without changing meaning?",
  "Is the interpretive compositional form <concept>(scene)[mode]{body} (operators.spw:105-110) meant as the designer-facing anatomy of a component, and could a probe test it?",
  "Can Spw operators carry valence spectra the way components do (valence-architecture.spw:47-83 'each component's boon is its way of opening'), and would that be a reading or a measure?",

   "why_it_fits": "Needs edges form a poset. A topological order is a valid syllabus, and the up-set of an open conjecture is exactly what loses its proof. proof-poset.spw shows this with GRH reaching only the Miller test."

   "why_it_fits": "This is the shape of Steen and Seebach or pi-Base: property tables plus implications. Closure derives facts, and the gaps it leaves are named questions."

  {
   "name": "Null-space bench: reaction balancer and Pi-group finder",
   "what_it_explores": "Balancing a reaction and finding dimensionless groups are one computation: the integer null space of a matrix (elements by species, or base dimensions by quantities). Atom conservation and dimensional homogeneity are the same linear constraint over different integer matrices.",
   "spw_sketch": "%sp.CH4{ C: 1, H: 4, name: \"methane\" }\n#>rxn_methane_combustion\n^[\"methane_combustion\"]{\n #:claim #!settled\n scheme: CH4 + O2 -> CO2 + H2O\n coefficients: #[ _, _, _, _ ]\n written: \"CH4 + 2 O2 -> CO2 + 2 H2O\"\n}\n%dim.pressure{ num: .{ M: 1 }, den: .{ L: 1, T: 2 }, si: \"Pa\" }\n#>eq_hydrostatic_missing_height\n^[\"hydrostatic_missing_height\"]{\n #:claim #!refuted\n statement: \"p = rho g\"\n lhs: .{ times: #[ dim.pressure ] }\n rhs: .{ times: #[ dim.density, dim.acceleration ] }\n}",
   "parses": true,

 "contraptions": [
  {
   "name": "Loop-sign walker",
   "what_it_explores": "Thomas's rules: a positive feedback circuit is necessary for multiple steady states, and a negative circuit is necessary for sustained oscillation. The walker collects signed bias edges, finds every simple cycle, and multiplies edge signs.",
   "spw_sketch": "#>life_p53\np53: .{ kind: #protein, gene: \"TP53\" }\n#>life_mdm2\nmdm2: .{ kind: #protein, gene: \"MDM2\" }\n^[\"edges\"]{\n =~\"./x1-loops.spw#life_p53\"[activates]{ ~\"./x1-loops.spw#life_mdm2\" }\n =~\"./x1-loops.spw#life_mdm2\"[inhibits]{ ~\"./x1-loops.spw#life_p53\" }\n}",
   "parses": true,
   "exists_today": "Partial. `spw select --selector bias` lists the edges (verified). Seed readBias, graphFromEdges and detectCycle exist (graph.ts:26, :76), but detectCycle reports one cycle and no signs. spw graph ignores bias edges. A scratch walker runs: life_clinical_tools/contraptions.mts.",
   "tooling_needed": "New. A loop-sign verb or formula family that enumerates simple cycles over readBias edges, with an axis-sign table declared in vocabulary.spw (activates +1, inhibits -1).",
   "wonder": "On pathway-sign-loops.spw it reports: p53/MDM2 has one inhibiting edge and a negative loop (can settle or oscillate); Cdk1/Cdc25 is positive (can switch); Cdk1/Wee1 is a double negative and therefore positive. Students see that two inhibitions make a switch. Stated limit: sign is necessary, not sufficient; switching also needs nonlinearity and oscillation needs delay."
  },
  {
   "name": "Band gap finder (Mendeleev for early-warning charts)",
   "what_it_explores": "Whether every reading a device can report lands in exactly one scoring band. It sorts the band spans for each observation and reports gaps and overlaps at the declared resolution and at ten times finer.",
   "spw_sketch": "#>band_temperature\n^[\"temperature\"]{\n unit: \"degrees C\"\n resolution: 0.1\n floor: .{ up_to: 35.0, points: 3 }\n low: .{ span: 35.1..36.0, points: 1 }\n normal: .{ span: 36.1..38.0, points: 0 }\n high: .{ span: 38.1..39.0, points: 1 }\n ceiling: .{ from: 39.1, points: 2 }\n}\nroute: ?match[total_band]{ \"low\" => ward_routine  \"medium\" => urgent_review  \"high\" => emergency_response }",
   "parses": true,
   "exists_today": "No CLI. The facets and .. ranges are already plain AST (Binding, Expression(..)). A scratch finder runs in contraptions.mts.",
   "tooling_needed": "New. A band-ladder checker that reads `resolution` and the span/up_to/from facets. The gate could call it on any surface whose form is registry or protocol.",
   "wonder": "On band-ladder.spw, the bands tile at the declared resolution, but every boundary leaves an unscored open interval at finer resolution: 36.05 C for temperature and 8.5 breaths per minute for respiratory rate. Rounding policy turns out to be part of the score. Stated limit: a Mendeleev gap predicts a missing element; a band gap predicts an unscored reading, not missing physiology."
  },
  {
   "name": "Gradient bench (compartments that decay, ions that keep a sign)",
   "what_it_explores": "Two linked questions. A dose moving between plasma and tissue on a discrete beat: how fast does it reach plateau, and does a loading dose shorten the wait? And for each ion, does recomputing the equilibrium potential from z and the two concentrations reproduce the expected sign, catching a minus that the parser would drop?",
   "spw_sketch": "^[\"sites\"]{\n plasma: .{ role: \"central compartment\", start: 0 }\n tissue: .{ role: \"peripheral compartment\", start: 0 }\n exchange: <>[plasma, tissue]\n half_life: .{ n: 6, unit: \"hours\" }\n beat: << decay ; diffuse ; inject >>\n}\n^[\"ions\"]{\n #>ion_k\n k: .{ z: \"+1\", out_mm: 5, in_mm: 140, expect_sign: \"minus\" }\n #>ion_cl\n cl: .{ z: \"-1\", out_mm: 110, in_mm: 10, expect_sign: \"minus\" }\n}",
   "parses": true,
   "exists_today": "Partial. Seed field.ts already has fieldBeat, halfLifeToRate, diffuseField and massConserved (field.ts:64, :75, :250, :274), tested under field-dynamics.spw:85-91. `spw formula --family field` finds the surface by pattern (verified: 8 hits). No command loads a surface's sites and parameters into fieldBeat. The Nernst calculation is scratch (life_clinical_tools/nernst.mts).",
   "tooling_needed": "New. A runner that maps facets to fieldBeat state and parameters, plus a small unit-and-sign checker for registry cells that reads z and concentration strings.",
   "wonder": "Verified runs. Diffusion conserves mass. With equal doses, troughs settle within 10 percent of plateau at beat 24; with a doubled first dose, at beat 6, so the loading-dose idea falls out of the arithmetic. The Nernst signs come out as K -89.0 mV, Na +66.5, Cl -64.0 and Ca +132.2, all as expected. Stated limits: fieldBeat decays every site, whereas the usual model eliminates only from the central compartment. Nernst describes one ion at equilibrium, not a resting potential."
  },

   "name": "Bundle audit (charted order against protocol precedence)",

   "parses": true,
   "exists_today": "No CLI. Stream nodes keep ';' and '||' as separators in the AST, so precedence can be read directly. A scratch audit runs in contraptions.mts.",
   "tooling_needed": "New. A schedule-to-precedence reader, with an audit verb that follows [audits_against] bias edges.",
   "wonder": "On protocol-aligner.spw, case_a breaks cultures-before-antibiotics and never charts vasopressors; case_b passes. Stated limits: a chart timestamp is documentation time, and the 2018 one-hour clock was revised in 2021, so every bundle is specific to its edition."
  }
 ],

 "architecture_recs": [
  "Before the health branch lands, extend vocabulary.spw axes.domain (line 31 allows only meta and matter) with life, health and neuro, each with a gloss. The gate currently fails #!health and #!life on every sketch (verified).",
  "Split the tree by scale, the way readers in this persona already think. Under life/: molecules, pathways, cells, tissues, organs, systems. Under health/: assessment, protocols, pharmacology, evidence, safety. Each index routes with ^[tree]{} (contract.spw:66) and opens with a ^[\"doors\"] frame naming separate entries for chart readers, bench scientists and modelers.",
  "Add registries/quantities/health.spw with scheme: population. Cells require unit, an interval or value, population, method or specimen, edition, src and status. Have the gate fail a health cell without a population, so a lab interval never reads as a constant of nature (reference-intervals.spw).",
  "Add registries/sources/health.spw in which every guideline names its body, edition and year, and editions are linked by supersedes edges (SSC 2018 to 2021), as contract.spw:108 requires.",
  "Declare a closed set of domain edge axes in vocabulary.spw (activates, inhibits, binds, catalyzes, transports, precedes, related_to, evidenced_by, differential, audits_against), kept separate from the surface relations at vocabulary.spw:44. The gate checks ^[edges] keys today, but not bias-edge axes. Pathway sign always goes in the axis, never in =bane.",
  "Add #:basis (proof, replicated_experiment, trial, observational, consensus, mechanism, case_report) and possibly #:strength to the statements vocabulary. Let source: accept a claim anchor whose frame carries its own source; the gate currently warns on this (verified).",
  "Gate additions: an AST lint for the twelve silent clinical shorthand forms, which currently pass everything (verified life_clinical_gate/meta/silent.spw), and a check that every health-domain surface carries ^[\"scope\"]{ not_clinical: ... }. contract.spw:107 requires this frame, but no gate rule enforces it.",
  "Put a hazards/false-friends surface at the health index and link it from every health surface's edges. Give it its own anchor per hazard, so a reviewer's correction can cite the exact rule.",
  "Put contraptions beside the claims they test, as probe_battery surfaces, and add a registry surface that lists each runnable checker with its command and its status. Use the status words of operators.spw:18-24: implemented, proposed, interpretive. A checker that only exists in scratch should say proposed.",
  "Write try kits for hands-on access (contract.spw:100-104): score NEWS2 from a vignette, build a paper p53/MDM2 loop and count inhibitions, layer two dyed compartments. Each kit names its safety line and the claim it demonstrates.",
  "Anchor naming: use lowercase slugs from HGNC symbols, with the official symbol as a string (gene: \"TP53\"). Spell out Greek letters. Prefix digit-led names. Use non-possessive eponyms in # title lines (contract.spw:44).",
  "Tooling outside the cut, flagged as needs tooling: spw graph should read readBias edges and strip fragments (theory_state F6), so a pathway surface renders as a graph. The validator should surface lexer errors (syntax_breadth F2)."
 ],
 "theory_questions": [
  "Should the lexer accept negative numbers? '-' is already a ConnectorKind (token.ts:26), but `-70` raises a hidden lexer error and binds 70, and physiology lives below zero.",
  "Should a bias edge carry sign apart from direction? Today =bane inverts direction (read-bias.ts:108), biologists will read it as inhibition, and the axis name is the only place sign can live.",
  "Should mood and case values be allowed to start with a digit? Evidence levels (1a), genes (53BP1) and receptors (5-HT) do, and #!1a silently splits into #, !, 1 and a.",
  "Is a care bundle a schedule or a set of precedence edges? Nested << >> covers only series-parallel orders. Should schedules admit general partial orders and cycles such as ADPIE, or are bias edges the canonical device for precedence?",

  "Deixis for #>. Holds: a mark points at what follows it. Observable: the particle binds to the next content node (canonical/particles.ts:4-7). Breaks: grammatical case is assigned by a governing head and marks a syntactic relation, while #:layer is an author-chosen attribute name with no head and no government. A key in an AVM is the closer analogy.",
  "Mood for #!. Holds: it 'asserts pragmatic force' (lexer/matchers/particles.ts:9-10), close to illocutionary force. Breaks: grammatical mood is a verbal inflection paradigm, and #! values mix epistemic status (#!settled) with genre (#!field_guide).",
  "Aspect for ~#. Holds: both concern time. Observable: census counts ~# as volatility, 'content expires' (canonical/particles.ts:110-113). Breaks: aspect is the internal temporal structure of an event, while expiring content is a property of the datum, closer to a stage-level predicate.",
  "Apposition for ~#( ). Holds: for nonrestrictive appositives the host means the same with or without it (apposition.spw:29). Observable: it is an Annotation beside its host (apposition.spw:91). Breaks: an appositive commits a speaker, while a Spw apposition has at most an author, and particles can bind to an apposition as if it were a host.",
  "Valence. Holds: nothing beyond the word. Breaks: valency counts a predicate's arguments (in Spw that is ONF arity, register-geometry.spw:56), while the Spw pentad is charge-neutral material quality (valence-architecture.spw:38-39).",
  "Particle stacks as proclitic clusters. Holds: rightward attachment and stacking of several marks on one host (verified with particleBindings). Breaks: clitics attach to a prosodic word under phonological conditions, while Spw particles attach by adjacency alone, across newlines, and to hosts as large as a whole frame.",
  "Labeled brackets and trees as ^ frames. Holds: nesting and labels are kept. Breaks: the cut says the tree is for finding, not for meaning (contract.spw:137). No dominance, c-command or headedness is computed, so syntactic relations cannot be read off the frame structure.",
  "Feature matrices as facets. Holds: attribute-value pairs (operators.spw:98). Breaks: there is no unification. Two facets with conflicting values sit side by side without failing, even though HOLE is described as a unification variable (token.ts:57).",
  "Feature cube. Holds: three binary features give a cube with eight corners. Breaks: real feature systems include multi-valued place, dependent features that apply only under others, and inventories that never fill their cube.",

   "name": "Mendeleev gap finder for a scope-and-sequence grid",
   "what_it_explores": "Which empty cells in a grade-band by strand curriculum grid can be predicted from their neighbors, and which are open invitations. By strand: properties 0.00, change 0.25, energy 0.50, models 0.50. Exactly one hole is sandwiched between filled cells in the same strand (g6_8.change), so it can be interpolated. g3_5.models is one-sided. k2.energy, k2.models, and g9_12.energy sit at the edge and are invitations.    "spw_sketch": "#>x_band_g6_8\n^[\"g6_8\"]{\n properties: .{ gist: \"density as mass divided by volume\", hands: 1 }\n change: _\n energy: .{ gist: \"thermal energy moves from warm to cool\", hands: 0 }\n}\n#>x_scope_gap_q\n?[\"Which empty cell can its neighbors predict?\"]{\n #:depth #!mathematical ~#lens(formal structure)\n !probe{ \"mark a hole sandwiched when the same strand is filled in the band before and after\" =id[p_x_scope_gap] =kind[calc] }\n breaks: \"strands share a committee decision, not a periodic law\"\n}",
